findings: scripts/agy_terminal_supervisor.py does not exist; architecture document explicitly describes design only.
Canonical AGY denial is unconditional and must remain unchanged. Calling the private process runner also invokes transport validation; it is not a local terminal route.
Broker wrapper forwards argv and inherits environment; it supplies no filesystem sandbox or ownership enforcement.

Python broker bridge has an environment allowlist, but executes in ROOT, has no filesystem isolation, accepts exit-zero fallback success without WorkResult, and timeout kills only direct process. It is not sufficient for this worker contract.

Existing _parse_agy_result enforces one init and final result, session consistency and normalized secret-checked WorkResult; it can be reused as a pure in-memory parser, not as native execution proof.
sandbox-exec and docker executable presence identifies local isolation candidates only; no provider, daemon, authentication or sandbox test ran.
concrete_missing_runtime_capabilities: Verified descendant-covering filesystem/process isolation with pinned executable and exact writable path manifest; temporary cwd and prompt ownership alone cannot enforce this.

Auth transport that lets the CLI use the existing selected account without exposing credential stores to generated commands or unrestricted descendant reads. An inherited AGY_HOME or unrestricted home mount is insufficient.
Dedicated supervisor with bounded stream capture, verified process/container ownership, deadline exit, orphan fencing and sanitized in-process result normalization.
Host-side reviewed-diff acceptance with base-content hash checks, path/type enforcement and no symlink/hardlink traversal; child cannot apply its own patch to shared workspace.

minimal_successor_scope.design_owner: business_analyst/orchestrator: explicitly bind separate local-only lifecycle and write manifest to existing user authorization; reconcile natural-exit-only policy without changing native gates
minimal_successor_scope.implementation_owner: developer or infrastructure-qualified worker: new scripts/agy_terminal_supervisor.py and narrowly scoped sandbox backend; no edit to canonical transport denial
minimal_successor_scope.qa_owner: qa_tester: new tests/test_agy_terminal_supervisor.py plus provider-free real sandbox negative probes before any AGY attempt
minimal_successor_scope.stage_1: Prove sandbox and auth boundary first. On failure stop SANDBOX_NOT_PROVEN or AUTH_ISOLATION_NOT_PROVEN; do not build a wrapper-only workaround.
minimal_successor_scope.stage_2: Create owner-only private source snapshot from explicit reviewed regular files, no git metadata, account state or secrets. Bind source hashes; permit writes/deletes only to owned paths, with directory-entry handling tested.
minimal_successor_scope.stage_3: Start one pinned selected-alias CLI through the new isolation backend with direct argv, minimal environment, fresh bound attempt/decision and deadline. Keep raw streams in bounded memory; normalize existing WorkResult v2, elide public streams, no native receipt claims.
minimal_successor_scope.stage_4: After child exit, reject unowned edits/deletions, special files, path escapes and stale base hashes. Independent reviewer validates patch before scoped host application. No child commit/push; cleanup only supervisor-owned temporary objects.

required_tests: Real denial of writes and deletion outside scope, shared workspace access, sensitive reads, symlink/hardlink and rename escape, descendant escape and inherited descriptor abuse.
Auth-session operation without child credential-file access; never log credentials or provider streams.
Exact path/hash admission, replay/expiry rejection, concurrent attempts, crash before/after spawn, owned deadline exit, PID reuse/orphan fencing.
Output overflow, duplicate final events, session mismatch, malformed/secret-bearing WorkResult, exit-zero invalid result and nonzero DONE rejected.
Patch allowlist, scoped deletion, stale host base, injected paths/special files, review-required acceptance and exact cleanup ownership.
Canonical AGY rejection remains unchanged; local receipts cannot satisfy native G/H or production identity gates.
recommended_next_action: Delegate provider-free sandbox/auth-boundary implementation and tests to a scoped worker. This is a concrete runtime prerequisite, not a request to repeat generic user approval. Do not invoke agy2 until enforcement passes.
residual_risk: Local sandbox and auth isolation remain unproven; no AGY work ran and executable presence proves neither capability nor account availability.
